advances: Finite balanced-menu structure and a one-group threshold. A rank-one group does not by itself pay other groups.

proof:
Restrict to the positive support of an extreme probability and let $V$ be the matrix of its vectors. The positive probability vector lies in $\ker V$. If the kernel had dimension at least two, it would contain a nonzero vector of coefficient sum zero, and small perturbations of both signs along it would preserve balance, total weight and nonnegativity. Extremality forbids this. Thus the kernel is one-dimensional, generated by a vector with every coordinate positive. No proper subset is dependent, since that would give a kernel vector with a zero entry. The support therefore has size one plus its rank, at most $d+1$. Positive column rescaling preserves the kernel dimension, proper-subset independence and existence of a positive dependence.

At rank one the circuit has two vectors, and their positive dependence forces opposite directions. Some probability weight is at least $1/2$, and Bernoulli's inequality gives $(1+1/d)^d\ge2$. At rank at least two any two collinear support vectors would be a dependent proper subset. Two normals supporting the same fiber facet must be collinear, giving the cap assertion. The rank-one payment at a single group is the one-atom assertion of outward-smoothed-response-atom-hinge-payment, whenever its positive-width conditions hold.

u_jv_j=0$ is nonempty. An extreme such probability has at most $d+1$ positive entries, and on its positive support the $v_j$ form a minimal positive linear circuit. Rescaling to $u_j$ preserves the circuit. At rank one there are two opposite continuous directions, with one response weight at least $1/2\ge\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. At rank at least two no directions on the support repeat or are antipodal. Consequently if these are continuous normals of ambient caps, at most one cap of that menu can support a given positive-area facet of a sampled fiber. The rank-one weight meets the one-group hinge threshold in the positive-width setting of outward-smoothed-response-atom-hinge-payment.
title: Positive circuits in extreme balanced finite response menus
